extracted.intended_audience: educators, school administrators, manual-training instructors, medical educators, physicians, and scientifically-minded public
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for running and judging manual-training schools, for scientifically assessing alleged 'thought-reading' phenomena, and for shaping medical education and the physician's future role. Covers instructional methods, scheduling, resources, costs, experimental controls, and the preventive/biological orientation of medicine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical skill demonstrated by completed workpieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Students should execute substantially the same set of pieces; quality and dexterity are judged by completed specimens (lead practice then hot-iron final), with instructor estimates stamped as percentages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work was first wrought in cold lead to study order and form, then executed in hot iron; specimens and tracings used for assessment; external practical smiths commented on workmanship (commendations and noted weaknesses such as fire management). Time-to-completion (e.g., pair of tongs in <4 hours) used as a performance marker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocated instructional hours and progression
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify total and weekly hours for shop instruction (example: blacksmithing ~200 hours total, ~10 hours/week for a second-year class).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides concrete scheduling: second-year blacksmithing occupied about 200 hours; students progressed from study in cold lead to hot iron work; such allocation is contrasted with far longer traditional apprenticeships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lesson length optimality
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange lesson duration to maximize interest and quality without tiring students (Mr. Foley: three-hour lessons preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-hour lessons 'create a vigorous interest without tiring' and produce more and better-quality work than four-hour lessons; shorter concentrated sessions leave more lasting impressions than physically taxing longer ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional sequence and practice method
rubrics_metrics.description: Use guided, stepwise practice—study steps and details (tracings, cold practice) before final execution in working material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example method: study pieces in cold lead to learn order and detail, then execute in hot iron; provide each student with his own forge and set of tools to practice individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of individual tools and workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip each pupil with a dedicated set of tools and workspace (e.g., individual forge) to ensure hands-on practice and dexterity acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes each man had his forge and set of tools; this enabled uniform practice and assessment across pupils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class size and instructor competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit divisions to manageable sizes (example: generally 20 members) and employ skilled mechanics who are also effective teachers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good mechanics who can teach are rare but essential; the school employed a first-class machinist and an expert blacksmith paid $1,200/year each; drawing classes may be occasionally doubled up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison of formal instruction to traditional apprenticeship
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether a concentrated, properly designed course (e.g., ~120 hours spread over ~40 days) can substitute for years of apprenticeship in producing dexterity and useful knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mr. Foley argued modern apprenticeship often yields little due to exploitative work assignments; a short, structured course can reach necessary dexterity quickly and more efficiently than multi-year shop service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of external expert evaluation (public exhibition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold public exhibitions and invite practical craftsmen to judge student work as an external quality check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At public exhibition, twenty boys worked at forges for two hours and practical smiths present highly commended the work; external observers noted specific weaknesses (e.g., fire management).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost accounting and per-pupil budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Document full capital and recurring costs (building, tools, lot) and estimate per-pupil annual costs for supplies and instruction (example totals shown: plant cost $63,400; supplies/instructions ~$75 per pupil next year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breakdown given: building ~$33,000; tools/furniture $16,000; lot $14,400; incidentals (wood, iron, wear/tear) ~$10/head; total supplies and instruction estimated at $75 per pupil. Warns reform is not immediately money-saving but a long-term investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional capacity and class structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan school capacity and multi-year class divisions (example: capacity ~240 boys in 1st/2nd/3rd-year classes of 100/80/60).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design implies progression across years and sizing of cohorts to match resources and pedagogical aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two implementation strategies for introducing manual training
rubrics_metrics.description: Either (1) incorporate a manual department into existing high schools by adjusting curricula, or (2) develop independent plans and solicit funding from wealthy public-spirited benefactors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues both methods viable: integrating into public schools will pay off and yield further growth; philanthropy (college-level benefactors) is another practical route, citing examples like Cornell and Johns Hopkins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment framing: long-term civic returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat manual training schools as a grand investment with social returns (reducing wasted expenditures on social disorder vs funding education).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes that spending on education is wiser and cheaper than spending on soldiers/police/property destruction; philanthropic satisfaction cited as testimony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaust known explanations before inferring new phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: In evaluating purported thought-reading, first exclude all known modes of explanation (muscular indication, collusion, signals) before considering unknown agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scientific method proceeds from known to unknown; common-sense demand that every known mode of explanation be exhausted; a priori arguments may supplement but empirical elimination of known causes is primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on personal integrity as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not accept accounts based on the 'good faith' or reputation of witnesses; require demonstrable, reproducible facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good character or not taking money does not preclude deception; scientific skepticism must depend on reproducible evidence rather than trust in individuals' honesty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for contact and sensory cues (blindfolding, silence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure subjects are truly isolated from physical contact and that auditory/visual cues are prevented (blindfolding and enforced silence) when testing for thought-reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many cases lacked blindfolding or silence; even facial expressions of an expectant circle can give unconscious indications; absence of such controls invalidates experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design to exclude collusion and coded signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Guard against prearranged codes and signaling systems between guider and sensitive (letters/words indicating categories, corrections conveying hints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple code can convey startling amounts of information; the child may be preinformed of object category so that initial guesses suffice to transmit further hints through corrections; 'undesigned coincidences' (mistaken guesses) suggest whispering or gesture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer independent observers and well-documented controlled trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Require experiments to be conducted under controlled conditions with independent observers and specific reporting of results obtained when the claimant was 'alone' or otherwise isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Family-presence experiments are untrustworthy; the paper notes lack of specific quotations of results from the 'alone' circumstances; ipse dixit of observers is insufficient; mental bias and faulty memory must be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skeptical interpretation of performances by children or close associates
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat performances by children and household servants as especially susceptible to collusion and trivial signaling; they are not strong evidence of inherited special faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Children readily join in deception; servant-girl association undermines claims of family-inherited clairvoyance; presence of father increasing success suggests collusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical education: firm grounding in anatomy, physiology, and biology
rubrics_metrics.description: Physicians must have full knowledge of human anatomy and physiology and be trained in biological sciences (including comparative anatomy/physiology) as the foundation for modern medicine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physiology has become nearly a separate science; understanding lower animals informs human structure and function; many advances (cell-life, parasitic etiology, experimental physiology) came from biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange medical curricula to teach essential biological truths without needless systematist detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure medical education so students grasp the great truths of animal and vegetable life without entanglement in valueless systematist minutiae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for curricular design that imparts fundamentals of biology necessary for clinical and preventive practice; quotes international opinion that medical training must be impregnated with biological fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize preventive medicine and sanitary science
rubrics_metrics.description: Orient physicians toward sanitary science, disease prevention, and public health measures (fresh air, drainage, clean food, clothing, exercise) rather than exclusive reliance on remedial drugs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanitary science leads medicine away from blind faith in therapeutics toward right living; doctors should teach people how to live; preventive measures can largely restrain epidemic and zymotic diseases and raise life expectancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use therapeutics sparingly and intelligently
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply drugs more sparingly and intelligently; depend more on hygienic means when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many top physicians now prescribe few or no drugs in some cases, relying on air, food, and sanitation; social habits and patient preferences (choosing pills over sanitary reform) limit physicians' effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physician as public educator, especially to women and households
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect physicians to instruct the community in hygienic laws and living—women especially—so they can manage homes, food, clothing, and child-rearing with medical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Women regulate the condition of the home and should have thorough medical education to teach others; the physician must undertake the task of educating the public despite slow uptake and prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize interplay between physical health and moral/ social conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that physical disorder often underlies moral and mental disorders and that preventive medicine can reduce crime and social ills to some extent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physician should consider moral pathology tied to bodily disease; be liberal and lenient in judgments where pathology may contribute to crime; preventive medicine may lessen criminality by improving health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground therapeutics and pathology in experimental methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Use experimental physiology to elucidate the action of medicaments and to inform therapeutics and pathology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professor Huxley's remark: discovery of parasitic etiology and experimental physiology are greatest steps toward scientific medicine; training in methods of experimental physiology is essential.
